test: none: open on SolidCraft's truck kernel (kernel work paused under tangency-labs/solidcraft#3992); geometry is the report's rectangle and the triage's 2 mm wall, reproduced on 0.19.0 in the issue's triage comment and on 0.29.0 with solidcraft-cli
summary: A chamfer on an inside (concave) corner edge of a thin rectangular ring was refused on SolidCraft's truck kernel with 'not supported yet: <d> mm is too large for this chamfer: the result changes N mm^3 of the part, more than the chamfer can (at most M mm^3)' (#4859), although the chamfer only fills the corner of the hole. The report: a 25 x 15 rectangle and its 2 mm offset extruded 10 mm, a 1 mm chamfer on the vertical edge picked at mid-height refused ('changes 28 mm^3, at most 6 mm^3'), 0.6 mm the largest that built (0.19.0). Triage on 0.19.0 rebuilt it as a 2 mm wall (25 x 15 less 21 x 11): the inside corner was refused at 2 mm, the outside corner built at 0.6, 1 and 2. Replayed with solidcraft-cli 0.29.0 (truck), the two rectangles sketched and extruded 10 as one ring (sketching the inside one as the outer rectangle's 2 mm inward offset gives the same), one corner chamfered: on the 2 mm wall the inside corner builds at 1 and 1.2 and is refused at 1.5, 1.9, 1.99, 2, 2.01, 2.5, 3 and 3.5, and builds again at 4; all four inside corners build at 1 and are refused at 2; on a 1 mm wall it builds at 0.6 and is refused at 0.8, 1 and 2, at 1 with exactly the report's message (changes 28 mm^3, at most 6 mm^3); on a 3 mm wall it is refused at 2, on a 4 mm wall it builds at 2 and 3, and the inside corner of a solid L block builds at 2 and 3; the outside corner of the 2 mm wall builds at 1, 2 and 3. So the refusal follows the wall thickness, which the chamfer's geometry does not depend on: the material it adds lies in the hole and never reaches the outer faces. Not fixed on truck: kernel work is paused (tangency-labs/solidcraft#3992) and the `pr` link is the SMLib kernel move (tangency-labs/solidcraft#4012). Geometry: the ring spans x 0..25, y 0..15, z 0..10 and its hole x w..25-w, y w..15-w, both loops counter-clockwise (the inner one is the hole, as in 4058-walls-joined-flush-round-a-floor.json). The chamfer step is solidcore's linear-section blend: on a right-angle edge between planes its leg on each face is `distance`, so each chamfered inside corner adds the triangular prism 0.5 d^2 * 10 in the corner of the hole, ending flat in the top and bottom faces, which are at right angles to the edge. Each edge is picked at mid-height, (w, w, 5) for the first. The cases keep d below half the hole's shorter side, so the chamfers stay apart. Volumes are closed form, checked by the shoelace area of the chamfered hole outline and by a randomised QMC over the ring less its hole plus the corner triangles, within two of its standard errors. Tolerance 1e-4 mm^3 (every result is a polyhedron), as in 3655-chamfer-all-box-edges-pick-order.json.
